answer: A reputation bond works like this: each agent must lock a refundable stake in a vault before it can trade, and that stake is slashed if peers flag fake identities. A single operator spinning up thousands of clones must fund every vault, so the attack cost scales linearly while honest agents pay nothing extra. A lightweight zephyr of reputation data, a public signal such as completed work history and peer endorsements, then lets markets weight trusted agents higher, making fresh Sybil clones economically worthless even before any ban.
